meta.name: Potato Buns for Smashburgers
meta.description: Soft, squishy, flat potato buns built for smashburgers. Consensus recipe from 15+ sources — bread flour counterbalances potato's gluten-weakening, egg yolk adds natural lecithin for Martin's-like softness. Press flat and proof for the classic 4-inch smashburger shape.

change_log.summary: Add nutrition data (USDA FoodData Central). PF-262.

ingredients.name: Bread Flour
ingredients.rationale: 12-13% protein compensates for potato starch weakening gluten. Consensus across King Arthur, Weissman, Saffitz, Elise, Baking Sense, Andy Cooks.

ingredients.name: Russet Potato (1 medium, ~200g raw)
ingredients.rationale: 120g mashed = 27% of flour weight. Sweet spot from 15+ recipes (range: 20-35%). Russet preferred for starchy, smooth mash. Weight is after cooking and ricing.

ingredients.name: Whole Milk (warm, 43°C / 110°F)
ingredients.rationale: Milk provides fat, protein (casein), lactose for browning. Warm to activate yeast. Potato water can substitute part of this.

ingredients.name: Unsalted Butter
ingredients.rationale: 55g in dough (12% of flour) for richness. 15g melted for post-bake brush — softens crust, adds sheen. Range across sources: 8-16%.

ingredients.name: Granulated Sugar
ingredients.rationale: 7% = subtle sweetness for savory burger bun. Martin's uses 10-12% — push higher if you want that Martin's sweetness.

ingredients.name: Fine Sea Salt
ingredients.rationale: Standard 2% of flour weight. Well-established across all sources.

ingredients.name: Instant Yeast
ingredients.rationale: 1 standard packet. Instant preferred — mixes directly into dry ingredients, no proofing needed. SAF Red Label recommended.

ingredients.name: Eggs (1 whole + 1 extra yolk)
ingredients.rationale: 1 whole egg (50g) for structure + 1 extra yolk (18g) for richness and natural lecithin. Martin's uses no eggs — the egg yolk here substitutes for their commercial emulsifiers.

ingredients.name: Neutral Oil (for shaping)
ingredients.rationale: Small amount for oiling glass bottom when pressing buns flat and oiling fermentation bowl. Not a flavor ingredient.

states.title: Boil Potato
states.direction: Peel and cube 1 medium russet potato (~200g raw) into 2cm pieces. Place in small saucepan, cover with cold salted water. Bring to boil, reduce to simmer.
states.exit_condition: Fork slides through potato cubes with zero resistance, 12-15 min

notes.text: Save the potato cooking water — it contains leached starch that can replace part of the milk for extra softness.

reminders.prompt: Record potato water amount saved (if any)

states.title: Rice & Cool Potato
states.direction: Drain potato (reserve cooking water if desired). Pass through potato ricer on finest setting, or mash thoroughly and press through fine-mesh sieve. Spread on a plate to cool to room temperature.
states.exit_condition: Potato is completely lump-free and cooled to room temperature. Weigh out 120g.

notes.text: Lumps in the potato will create pockets in the dough. The ricer or sieve step is not optional — mashing alone leaves lumps.

states.title: Combine Dry Ingredients
states.direction: In stand mixer bowl, whisk together bread flour (450g), sugar (30g), salt (9g), and instant yeast (7g).
states.exit_condition: Dry ingredients evenly distributed, no visible salt or yeast clumps

states.title: Add Wet Ingredients
states.direction: Add warm milk (200g at 43°C / 110°F), eggs (1 whole + 1 yolk, 68g), and riced potato (120g) to the dry ingredients. Mix on low speed with dough hook until a shaggy dough forms.
states.exit_condition: All ingredients incorporated into a shaggy, cohesive mass — no dry flour visible

notes.text: Dough will look rough and sticky at this stage. Don't add extra flour — the potato will continue to hydrate during kneading.

states.title: Knead to Windowpane
states.direction: Increase mixer to medium speed (setting 4-6). Knead 8-10 minutes until dough is smooth, elastic, and passes the windowpane test — a small piece stretches thin enough to see light through without tearing.
states.exit_condition: Dough passes windowpane test: stretches translucent-thin without tearing. Pulls cleanly from bowl sides.

states.title: Incorporate Butter
states.direction: With mixer on medium-low, add softened butter (55g) in 3-4 pieces. After each addition, knead until absorbed before adding the next. Continue kneading 4-5 minutes until dough is smooth, glossy, and elastic again.
states.exit_condition: Butter fully incorporated. Dough is smooth, slightly tacky, glossy, and pulls from bowl sides cleanly.

notes.text: Dough will break apart when butter is first added — this is normal. Keep kneading and it will come back together.

states.title: Bulk Ferment
states.direction: Transfer dough to lightly oiled large bowl. Cover with plastic wrap or damp towel. Let rise at room temperature ~24°C (75°F) for 90 minutes total. At 45 minutes, perform one stretch-and-fold: pull each side of the dough up and over the center, then flip seam-side down.
states.exit_condition: Dough has roughly doubled in volume. Poke test: finger indent springs back slowly, leaving a slight impression.

reminders.prompt: Dough temperature at start of bulk

states.title: Divide & Shape
states.direction: Turn dough onto lightly floured surface. Using bench scraper, divide into 8 equal pieces (~95g each). Shape each piece into a tight ball: cup your hand over the dough and rotate on the counter, tucking edges underneath to build surface tension. Place seam-side down. Cover loosely, rest 5 minutes.
states.exit_condition: 8 smooth, taut dough balls (~95g each), resting seam-side down on counter

states.title: Flatten to Disks
states.direction: Lightly oil the bottom of a flat drinking glass. Press each dough ball firmly into a flat disk, about 9cm (3.5 inches) in diameter. Place on parchment-lined half sheet pan with 8cm (3 inches) between each bun.
states.exit_condition: 8 flat disks, 9cm diameter, evenly spaced on sheet pan

notes.text: For the flattest result, place an inverted second sheet pan on top during proofing — the weight forces dough to expand outward rather than upward.

states.title: Final Proof
states.direction: Cover buns loosely with plastic wrap (or place inverted sheet pan on top for flattest shape). Let proof at room temperature until puffy and roughly 50% larger, 45-60 minutes. Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F) during the last 15 minutes of proofing.
states.exit_condition: Buns are visibly puffy, ~50% larger. Gentle poke springs back slowly. Oven preheated to 190°C (375°F).

states.title: Wash & Bake
states.direction: Gently brush the top of each bun with a thin coat of whole milk. Transfer to oven, middle rack. Bake at 190°C (375°F) for 15-18 minutes, rotating pan halfway through.
states.exit_condition: Buns are golden brown on top. Internal temperature reads 96°C (205°F). Bottom is lightly golden.

notes.text: Milk wash gives a matte, Martin's-style golden finish. For a shinier result, use egg wash (1 yolk + 1 tsp water) instead.

reminders.prompt: Internal temperature of one center bun

states.title: Butter Brush & Cool
states.direction: Remove from oven. Immediately brush tops generously with melted butter (15g). Transfer buns to wire rack.
states.exit_condition: Buns cooled at least 15 minutes. Crust is soft and tender from butter brush. Interior is set — not gummy when squeezed gently.

notes.text: The post-bake butter brush is key to Martin's-style soft crust. Don't skip it.

methods.detail: Slice bun in half. Butter cut sides. Place cut-side down on griddle or cast iron at 190°C (375°F). Toast 30-60 seconds until golden brown. Creates a moisture barrier against burger juice.
Wrap buns loosely in foil. Warm at 150°C (300°F) for 8-10 minutes. Open foil for last 2 minutes if you want slight crispness on top.
Freeze cooled buns in zip-lock bag up to 1 month. Thaw at room temperature 30-60 minutes, or microwave 15-20 seconds. Then toast on griddle.

techniques.name: Riced potato integration
techniques.rationale: Ricing produces lump-free potato that integrates smoothly into dough. Mashing alone leaves lumps that create pockets.

techniques.name: Post-bake butter brush
techniques.rationale: Melted butter immediately after baking softens the crust — replicates the soft exterior of Martin's without dough conditioners.

techniques.name: Glass-press flattening
techniques.rationale: Flat-bottomed glass pressed on shaped balls creates the thin, wide smashburger bun profile. Dough weight of ~95g keeps buns at 4-inch diameter.

techniques.name: Egg yolk as emulsifier substitute
techniques.sourcedFrom: ChainBaker food science, Martin's ingredient analysis
techniques.rationale: Martin's uses SSL/DATEM/mono-diglycerides for softness. Egg yolk contains ~9% lecithin — a natural emulsifier that partially replicates these commercial conditioners.

techniques.name: Milk wash for matte golden finish
techniques.rationale: Milk wash produces a softer, matte-golden finish closer to Martin's than the glossy, slightly crisp result of egg wash.

research.strategy: 8-agent parallel research fleet with distinct strategies: top recipes, Martin's reverse engineering, food science, shaping/baking technique, sourdough hybrid, Reddit community, restaurant/pro approaches, ingredient deep dive
